```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

**magic.table** wraps an ordinary data frame so that the columns you *derive* from
it aren't computed and thrown away — they're **recorded as the expressions that
produced them**. You can then export the table to a spreadsheet where those
derived columns land as **live formulas**, not pasted-in numbers. Edit a source
cell in the sheet and the derived cells recompute, because they really are
`=`-formulas.

This walkthrough builds a small table, records two derived columns, inspects
their provenance, and writes two spreadsheet artifacts you can open or paste — no
Google account, no auth, no token.

## Install

```{r}
#| eval: false
#| purl: false
remotes::install_github("jessebrandtdata/magic.table")
```

```{r}
#| label: library
library(magic.table)
library(dplyr)
```

## Start with a plain data frame

Any data frame will do. We take the first six cars from `mtcars`, keeping a
readable label column and a few numeric columns to compute on.

```{r}
#| label: data
cars <- head(mtcars, 6)
df <- data.frame(
  car = rownames(cars),
  mpg = cars$mpg,
  hp  = cars$hp,
  wt  = cars$wt,
  cyl = cars$cyl
)
df
```

## Make it a magic.table

`magic.table()` wraps the data frame. Nothing about your data changes — you've
just switched on *recording*.

```{r}
#| label: wrap
mt <- magic.table(df)
mt
```

## Record derived columns with `mutate()`

Here's the twist: `mutate()` on a magic.table does **not** compute. It *records*
each expression. `power_to_weight` is plain arithmetic across two columns;
`mpg_vs_avg` is a ratio against the column mean (more on that aggregate below).

```{r}
#| label: mutate
mt <- mt |>
  mutate(
    power_to_weight = hp / wt,
    mpg_vs_avg      = mpg / mean(mpg)
  )
mt
```

Notice the printout still reports the two recorded ops — the values haven't been
materialized yet.

## See the provenance

`provenance()` is what "recorded computation" buys you: for every column it tells
you whether it's an original `source` column or one `computed` from an
expression — and hands you that expression back. This is derived on demand; no
extra state is stored.

```{r}
#| label: provenance
provenance(mt)
```

## Teach the dialect a new function

The built-in translator turns a bare column reference into the **current row's**
cell (`mpg` → `B2` on row 2), so on its own it can't express an aggregate over a
whole column. `register_sheet_translator()` is the extension point: we teach it
that `mean(col)` should become an absolute-range `AVERAGE`.

```{r}
#| label: translator
start_row      <- 1L                       # header row
data_first_row <- start_row + 1L           # first data row
data_last_row  <- data_first_row + nrow(df) - 1L

register_sheet_translator("mean", function(args, ctx) {
  col <- sub("[0-9]+$", "", args[[1]])     # "B2" -> "B"
  sprintf("AVERAGE(%s$%d:%s$%d)", col, data_first_row, col, data_last_row)
})
```

## Materialize the A1 formula grid

`as_sheet_cells()` walks the recorded ops and produces exactly what would be
written to a sheet — original columns keep their values, derived columns become
`=`-formulas anchored at `start_row`. No network, no auth.

```{r}
#| label: cells
cells <- as_sheet_cells(mt, start_row = start_row)
cells
```

A live-formula summary row (column averages) is built the same way, via
`make_summary_row()`:

```{r}
#| label: summary
summary <- make_summary_row(
  df,
  data_start_row = data_first_row,
  label          = "Average",
  fn             = "AVERAGE"
)
summary
```

## Write the two spreadsheet artifacts

### `demo-formulas.xlsx` — real embedded formulas (openxlsx)

The working, token-free export backend: `openxlsx::writeFormula()` embeds each
`=`-formula into a local `.xlsx` that Excel (or Google Sheets, via import)
recalculates on open.

```{r}
#| label: xlsx
strip_eq <- function(x) sub("^=", "", x)       # openxlsx wants no leading "="

wb <- openxlsx::createWorkbook()
openxlsx::addWorksheet(wb, "Demo")

# Literal data: header row 1 + values rows 2..7, columns A..E.
openxlsx::writeData(wb, "Demo", df, startRow = 1L, startCol = 1L, colNames = TRUE)
# Derived-column headers (F, G) + their formulas down rows 2..7.
openxlsx::writeData(
  wb, "Demo",
  as.data.frame(as.list(names(cells)[6:7]), stringsAsFactors = FALSE),
  startRow = 1L, startCol = 6L, colNames = FALSE
)
openxlsx::writeFormula(wb, "Demo", strip_eq(as.character(cells$power_to_weight)),
                       startCol = 6L, startRow = 2L)
openxlsx::writeFormula(wb, "Demo", strip_eq(as.character(cells$mpg_vs_avg)),
                       startCol = 7L, startRow = 2L)
# Summary row (row 8): label in A, AVERAGE formulas in B..E.
openxlsx::writeData(wb, "Demo", "Average", startRow = 8L, startCol = 1L,
                    colNames = FALSE)
summary_col <- c(mpg = 2L, hp = 3L, wt = 4L, cyl = 5L)
for (nm in names(summary_col)) {
  openxlsx::writeFormula(wb, "Demo", strip_eq(as.character(summary[[nm]])),
                         startCol = summary_col[[nm]], startRow = 8L)
}
openxlsx::saveWorkbook(wb, "demo-formulas.xlsx", overwrite = TRUE)
```

### `demo-paste.tsv` — copy-paste route

The same grid as tab-separated text, formula cells as literal `=...` strings, so
you can paste it straight into a sheet.

```{r}
#| label: tsv
stringify   <- function(x) vapply(x, as.character, character(1))
grid        <- as.data.frame(lapply(cells, stringify), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
summary_row <- stats::setNames(rep("", ncol(cells)), names(cells))
for (nm in names(summary)) summary_row[[nm]] <- as.character(summary[[nm]])

block <- rbind(stats::setNames(as.list(names(cells)), names(cells)), grid, summary_row)
write.table(block, "demo-paste.tsv", sep = "\t", quote = FALSE,
            row.names = FALSE, col.names = FALSE, na = "")
```

## Now open it / paste it

- **Excel / LibreOffice:** open `demo-formulas.xlsx`. Formulas recalculate on open.
- **Google Sheets (import):** New sheet → *File ▸ Import ▸ Upload* `demo-formulas.xlsx`.
- **Google Sheets / Excel (paste):** open a blank sheet, click cell **A1**, paste
  `demo-paste.tsv`. The paste target **must be A1** so the relative references
  (`B2`, `C2`, …) line up.

The derived cells should evaluate to these (computed eagerly in R for comparison):

```{r}
#| label: expected
expected <- data.frame(
  car             = df$car,
  power_to_weight = round(df$hp / df$wt, 4),
  mpg_vs_avg      = round(df$mpg / mean(df$mpg), 4)
)
expected

round(sapply(df[c("mpg", "hp", "wt", "cyl")], mean), 4)  # the "Average" row
```

If those match what the sheet shows, the offline translation is faithful — and
every derived cell is a live formula, so editing a source number recomputes it.
